neighbours.label: the word just before a childhood life-stage phrase ('as' in 'as a child', 'were' in 'when we were kids'): anticipating childhood
fire: I read every comic I could find as a child.
My sister and I built forts in the woods when we were kids.
He broke his arm twice as a teenager.
Back when I was small, my father worked nights at the mill.
She learned to swim in the lake as a little girl.
We spent hours fishing off the dock when we were young.
I was terrified of thunderstorms as a kid.
Like many people, he collected stamps as a boy.
quiet: I read every report I could find as a journalist.
My sister and I built a shed in the garden last spring.
He broke his arm twice while playing rugby last season.
These days my father works nights at the hospital.
She learned to swim in the lake as part of her training.
We spent hours fishing off the dock during the holiday.
I was terrified of thunderstorms during the flight.
Like many people, he works as a volunteer on weekends.
